answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds lock staking collateral into a time-varying deposit whose expected return is calibrated to the marginal cost to forge a Sybil identity. A subgame-perfect punishment matrix enforces slashing penalties proportional to the verifiable delay proved by zero-knowledge proofs, rendering the expected attack utility strictly negative. Under the resulting hollow tide of credible threats, rational agents converge to a strict Nash equilibrium where any identity multiplication yields a loss exceeding the bonded stake.
